paragraphs: Scientists at Maynooth University are making a new shoe insole. An insole is the soft part inside a shoe. It may help people with a skin condition called EB.
People with EB get painful blisters very easily. Heat and sweat make it worse. When they walk, their feet get hot.
The new insole keeps the foot cool. Cold liquid moves through it. It keeps the foot at 32 degrees.
Dr Linzi Ryan leads the team. A family from Meath tried the new design. Mark and Sophia Dawson both have EB.
About 300 people in Ireland get help from a charity called Debra. The charity says the insole is not a cure. But it could make life easier.

冷的液體會在裡面流動。
它讓腳維持在32度。
琳茲．萊恩博士帶領這個團隊。
一個來自米斯郡的家庭試用了新設計。
馬克和蘇菲亞．道森都患有EB。
愛爾蘭約有300人接受一個叫Debra的慈善機構幫助。
這個慈善機構說鞋墊並不能治癒疾病。
但它能讓生活變得更輕鬆。

paragraphs: Researchers at Maynooth University are developing a special shoe insole for people with a rare skin condition. The condition is called epidermolysis bullosa, or EB, and it makes the skin very easy to damage.

The insole is designed for people with EB simplex, the most common type. In these people, a protein that holds the layers of skin together is missing. Heat, sweat and rubbing then cause painful blisters. Feet have many sweat glands, so walking often makes the problem worse.
The insole moves a cool liquid under the foot to keep it at 32 degrees. A small part outside the shoe takes the heat away. It does not heal blisters, but it aims to stop them from forming.

Dr Linzi Ryan, who leads the research, showed the latest model to the Dawson family from Co Meath. Mark and Sophia Dawson both have EB. Mr Dawson said the insole could help many people who suffer in silence.

The charity Debra supports about 300 people with EB in Ireland. Some of them put frozen pads in their shoes before a short walk. Debra's head of research said the insole was not a cure, but it could remove one barrier from daily life.
sentZh: 梅努斯大學的研究人員正在為患有一種罕見皮膚疾病的人開發特殊鞋墊。
這種疾病叫做大皰性表皮鬆解症，簡稱EB，它讓皮膚非常容易受傷。
這種鞋墊是為最常見類型的單純型EB患者設計的。
這些患者缺少一種把皮膚各層連在一起的蛋白質。
於是熱、汗和摩擦就會造成疼痛的水泡。
腳上有很多汗腺，所以走路常會讓問題更嚴重。
鞋墊讓冷卻液在腳底下流動，使腳維持在32度。
鞋子外面有一個小零件會把熱帶走。
它不能治好水泡，但目的是防止水泡形成。
帶領研究的琳茲．萊恩博士把最新型號展示給來自米斯郡的道森一家。
馬克和蘇菲亞．道森都患有EB。
道森先生說這種鞋墊能幫助許多默默受苦的人。
慈善機構Debra在愛爾蘭支援約300名EB患者。
其中有些人在短程散步前會把冷凍墊放進鞋裡。
Debra的研究主管說，這種鞋墊不能治癒疾病，但能為日常生活除去一個障礙。

paragraphs: Researchers at Maynooth University are developing a cooling shoe insole that could prevent painful blisters in people living with a form of the genetic skin condition epidermolysis bullosa (EB).

The device targets EB simplex, the most common type, in which a missing protein fails to bind the layers of skin together. Combined with heat, moisture and friction, this leads to blistering, and because feet contain a large number of sweat glands, simply walking can trigger it.

The insole circulates a cooling fluid to keep the foot at around 32 degrees, while a separate heat exchanger outside the shoe draws heat away. It is not a treatment, but is intended to stop blisters forming in the first place, and it will eventually be sold commercially.

Research lead Dr Linzi Ryan recently presented the latest prototype to the Dawson family in Co Meath, where Mark and Sophia both have the condition. Mr Dawson said it could benefit people who suffer in silence, while Dr Ryan noted that EB simplex is often hidden but can affect social life and confidence.

Debra, the national EB charity, supports around 300 people in Ireland. Its head of research, Fatma Ben Yousseff, called the project a potential game changer, stressing that it is not a cure but removes one more barrier. The work is funded by Debra and EB Research in Austria.
sentZh: 梅努斯大學的研究人員正在開發一種降溫鞋墊，可望預防一種遺傳性皮膚疾病大皰性表皮鬆解症（EB）患者長出疼痛的水泡。
這種裝置針對最常見的單純型EB，患者因缺少某種蛋白質，皮膚各層無法緊密結合。
再加上熱、濕氣和摩擦，就會導致起水泡，而且由於腳上有大量汗腺，光是走路就可能引發。
鞋墊讓冷卻液循環，使腳維持在約32度，而鞋外另有一個熱交換器把熱導走。
它並不是治療方法，而是要從一開始就阻止水泡形成，最終也會在市面上販售。
研究負責人琳茲．萊恩博士最近向米斯郡的道森一家展示了最新原型，家中的馬克和蘇菲亞都患有此病。
道森先生說它能讓默默受苦的人受益，萊恩博士則指出，單純型EB常不易察覺，卻可能影響社交生活與自信。
全國性EB慈善機構Debra在愛爾蘭支援約300人。
其研究主管法特瑪．本．尤塞夫稱這項計畫可能改變局面，並強調它不是治癒方法，但能再消除一道障礙。
這項研究由Debra和奧地利的EB Research資助。

paragraphs: Researchers at Maynooth University are devising a cooling shoe insole that could spare people with a form of the skin disorder epidermolysis bullosa (EB) from debilitating blisters.

The device is aimed at EB simplex, the most prevalent variant, in which the absence of a key protein leaves the layers of skin poorly bound. Heat, moisture and friction then conspire to produce blisters, and since the feet are densely packed with sweat glands, even an ordinary stroll can set them off.

The insole channels a cooling fluid beneath the sole to hold the foot at roughly 32 degrees, while an external heat exchanger dissipates the excess warmth. Rather than treating blisters, it is designed to forestall them altogether, and it is ultimately destined for the commercial market.

Dr Linzi Ryan, who spearheads the project, unveiled the latest prototype to the Dawson family in Co Meath, two of whom, Mark and Sophia, live with the condition. Mr Dawson remarked that it could transform life for those who suffer in silence.

Debra, the national EB charity, which supports some 300 people in Ireland, hailed the device as a potential game changer. Its head of research, Fatma Ben Yousseff, cautioned that it was no cure, but said it would remove yet another obstacle. The research has been seed-funded by Debra and EB Research in Austria.
sentZh: 梅努斯大學的研究人員正在設計一種降溫鞋墊，可望讓某類型皮膚疾病大皰性表皮鬆解症（EB）的患者免受使人虛弱的水泡之苦。
這種裝置針對最普遍的單純型EB，患者因缺乏一種關鍵蛋白質，皮膚各層結合不牢。
熱、濕氣和摩擦於是共同造成水泡，而由於腳部汗腺密布，就連普通的散步也可能引發。
鞋墊在腳底下導引冷卻液，使腳保持在約32度，外部的熱交換器則散去多餘的熱量。
它並非用來治療水泡，而是設計來徹底預先防止水泡，最終也將推向商業市場。
主導這項計畫的琳茲．萊恩博士向米斯郡的道森一家揭曉了最新原型，其中馬克和蘇菲亞兩人患有此病。
道森先生表示，它能徹底改變那些默默受苦者的生活。
在愛爾蘭支援約300人的全國性EB慈善機構Debra，盛讚這項裝置可能扭轉局面。
其研究主管法特瑪．本．尤塞夫提醒它並非治癒方法，但表示它能再移除一道障礙。
這項研究獲得Debra和奧地利EB Research的種子資金。

paragraphs: Researchers at Maynooth University are developing a cooling shoe insole that may substantially reduce blistering among individuals with a form of the dermatological condition epidermolysis bullosa (EB).

The device is designed for EB simplex, the most prevalent subtype, in which the absence of a particular protein compromises the bonding between layers of skin. When combined with heat, moisture and friction, this deficiency results in blistering; consequently, since the feet contain a high concentration of sweat glands, routine walking frequently triggers symptoms.

The insole circulates a cooling fluid in order to maintain the foot at approximately 32 degrees, while an external heat exchanger dissipates excess heat. Although it does not constitute a treatment, it is intended to prevent blisters from developing, and it is expected to be commercially available in due course.

The research lead, Dr Linzi Ryan, recently demonstrated the latest prototype to the Dawson family in Co Meath, two of whose members, Mark and Sophia, have the condition. She emphasised that EB simplex is frequently invisible to others, yet it can significantly undermine social participation and self-confidence.

Debra, the national EB charity, which supports approximately 300 individuals in Ireland, described the innovation as potentially transformative. Nevertheless, its head of research, Fatma Ben Yousseff, emphasised that it is not a cure, although it would eliminate one further barrier. Notably, if the insole were classified as a medical device, it would become considerably more accessible.

這種裝置是為最普遍的亞型單純型EB設計，患者因缺乏某種特定蛋白質，皮膚層之間的結合受到損害。
這種缺陷再加上熱、濕氣和摩擦，就會導致起水泡；因此，由於腳部汗腺高度集中，日常走路往往就會引發症狀。
鞋墊讓冷卻液循環，使腳維持在約32度，外部的熱交換器則散去多餘熱量。
雖然它不算是一種治療，但目的在於防止水泡產生，預計將在適當時候於市面上推出。
研究負責人琳茲．萊恩博士最近向米斯郡的道森一家示範了最新原型，家中馬克和蘇菲亞兩人患有此病。
她強調，單純型EB往往不為他人所見，卻可能嚴重削弱社交參與和自信心。
在愛爾蘭支援約300人的全國性EB慈善機構Debra形容這項創新可能帶來重大轉變。
然而，其研究主管法特瑪．本．尤塞夫強調它並非治癒方法，不過能再消除一道障礙。
值得注意的是，如果這種鞋墊被歸類為醫療器材，取得將會容易得多。
